note: The healed student with its learned routers picking 16 and 32 of the 64 routed experts instead of 9, on section 19's multiple-choice benchmark (slim_bench.py with arms healed_k16 and healed_k32), written 2026-11-01 before the run. The user: 'should we just switch from 9 experts to 16 and see if that fixes a bunch?' No training: the adapter and routers are the healing run's, trained at 9, so these are lower bounds for a model healed at that count. Local GPU, no pod. Generations at 16 are in opd_k16_rules.json.
design: Section 19's rows, prompts and scoring (rows rebuilt by prepare in this folder and checked identical to bench/'s). After the reproduction check at 9 experts, the healed student is scored with its learned routers picking the top 16, then the top 32, of the 64 routed experts. Per layer that runs 1,536 shared + 16 x 168 = 4,224 of 12,288 MLP neurons (34%; about 3.4B parameters per token against 2.95B), then 1,536 + 32 x 168 = 6,912 (56%; about 4.5B). The report compares them with section 19's arms (earlier: bench).
reading: Each count against 9 (share of the dense model's accuracy above chance, averaged over the four tests: 0.45) and against Qwen3.5-2B (0.68). If 16 experts keep at least 0.7, most of what the 25% model lost on these tests comes back with a third of the neurons, even without healing at that count. If 16 stays near 9 and only 32 recovers, the knowledge needs over half of the MLP per token, and a 25-35% budget cannot hold it without much more training. Every-neuron (all 64) is section 19's 1.08.
